# Both sides of a secret merge are checked against the audit log of the branch
# they come from, not just the incoming one.
#
# That distinction only shows up in a rebase. `git merge`, cherry-pick, revert and
# stash pop put our own history on %A, but a rebase (`git pull --rebase` included)
# replays our commits ON TOP of the upstream, so HEAD - and with it %A - is the
# side we did not write. Checking only %B would leave exactly that side unchecked.
#
# The object below is the one merge_rejects_foreign_object_workflow refuses on the
# incoming side: it decrypts (same recipient) but is signed by a key this repo's
# log never pinned. Were it merged, its content would end up inside an object
# resealed under our own key - and the reseal repairs the root hash, so a later
# `sesam verify` would no longer have anything to catch it with.

sesam-repo admin base.txt mine.txt other.txt

cp $TMPDIR/base.txt s
exec sesam add s --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add s'

# A second, unrelated sesam repo, initialized with the same identity: its object
# is encrypted to us (so it decrypts) but signed by its own key (so it means
# nothing here).
mkdir $TMPDIR/foreign
cd $TMPDIR/foreign
exec git init
exec git config user.email test@sesam.dev
exec git config user.name 'Sesam Test'
exec sesam init --user admin
cp $TMPDIR/other.txt s
exec sesam add s --group admin
cd $WORK

# UPSTREAM: the attacker pushed the foreign object onto the branch we track. The
# audit log is untouched, so nothing about the vault state looks off.
cp $TMPDIR/foreign/.sesam/objects/s.sesam .sesam/objects/s.sesam
exec git add .sesam/objects/s.sesam
exec git commit --no-verify -m 'upstream: foreign object'

# OURS: a local change to the same line, branched off before the poisoned commit.
exec git checkout -b topic HEAD~1
cp $TMPDIR/mine.txt s
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'topic: my change'

# Refused, and the message says which side is at fault: during a rebase "ours" is
# the branch being rebased onto, which is the surprising part.
! exec git rebase master
stderr 'our s does not verify against this repository''s audit log'
stderr 'rebasing onto'
stderr 'no matching signature key found'
! stderr 'automatically merging revealed file s'

# Nothing of theirs was written: the revealed file still holds our own content,
# with no merge markers and no trace of the foreign side.
exec git rebase --abort
exec cat s
stdout 'MINE'
! stdout 'FOREIGN'
! grep '^<<<<<<< ' s

-- base.txt --
line one
line two
line three
-- mine.txt --
line one
MINE
line three
-- other.txt --
line one
FOREIGN
line three
